resources.string: How the fibula helps frame the ankle
Normal ankle anatomy in simplified front and side views. Very small motions of the fibula are enlarged for visibility. Angles and distances are not measurements.
The thinner bone on the outside of the lower leg is the fibula. Its lower end extends beside the talus and contributes the outer wall of the ankle frame.
The lower tibia and fibula surround the top of the talus. The ligament connection between the two lower-leg bones keeps them together while allowing small adjustments.
In this side view, the foot tips upward as the talus moves relative to the lower leg. The side view shows the large direction of movement, not the full joint motion.
As the ankle bends upward, the lower fibula can shift and rotate slightly. The drawing enlarges one sideways component to make it visible.
The foot returns toward its starting position. The talus remains within the ankle frame as the two lower-leg bones adjust together.
